final_message:
I fixed it with two changes in `fiscal/calendar.py`. All 18 tests pass now; before the fix, 8 failed.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Early-February sales landed in the wrong fiscal year | `_nearest_saturday` always went back to the Saturday on or before Jan 31, so a year could never end in February. For example, FY2024 ended Jan 25, 2025 instead of Feb 1. | It now takes the Saturday within 3 days of Jan 31, earlier or later, as SPEC.md §1 says. |
| 53-week years looked wrong | The extra week was added to period 1, but SPEC.md §4 says it belongs to period 12. The wrong year-end also meant some years weren't detected as 53-week years at all. | The extra week now goes to period 12. |

`fiscal_week` and `period_bounds` were already correct. They were giving wrong answers only because they rely on the two functions above.

As a sanity check, 2017, 2023 and 2028 are the only 53-week years between 2015 and 2029. Each ends on Feb 3 of the following year, which matches the standard NRF 4-5-4 calendar.

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
Ran 18 tests in 0.001s
OK
exit=0
```

I didn't touch any tests. I recorded the result with `hc claim` (one claim for the file change, one for the passing tests). Nothing is committed yet; tell me if you want me to commit it.
